activities.title: Membrane structure and movement

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because hydrophobic interior limits many polar or charged substances.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.

activities.label: Explain the model
activities.title: Explain the membrane idea
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain why the membrane is selective and how transport can differ by energy use.
activities.concept: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because hydrophobic interior limits many polar or charged substances
activities.correctAnswer: The phospholipid bilayer has a hydrophobic interior that blocks many polar or charged substances, so the membrane is selectively permeable.
activities.feedback: A complete answer states that the hydrophobic interior limits some substances and connects that to selective permeability.

activities.label: Fix the gap
activities.title: Repair the transport explanation
activities.body: Revise your answer using the correct energy rule. Keep it to one or two sentences.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Confusing passive transport with active transport by treating any movement across the membrane as energy-requiring.
activities.concept: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport use
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves down a concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport requires energy to move against the gradient.
activities.feedback: The key repair is to separate movement down the gradient from movement against it and link only the second one to energy.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: Explain it again
activities.body: Explain the full idea again in plain language without copying the model.
activities.concept: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport use
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down the concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
activities.feedback: A strong answer now includes the direction of movement and the energy difference.

activities.label: Check the model
activities.title: Classify one transport choice
activities.body: Choose the best answer for a membrane transport situation.
activities.concept: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport use
choices: A molecule moves from high concentration to low concentration without ATP.
A molecule moves from low concentration to high concentration using ATP.
A molecule stays outside the cell because the membrane is never selective.
A molecule changes into another substance before crossing the membrane.
activities.correctAnswer: A molecule moves from high concentration to low concentration without ATP.
activities.feedback: Movement down a gradient without ATP is passive transport; movement against a gradient with energy is active transport.

check.title: Why Membranes Restrict Solutes
check.prompt: How does phospholipid structure make the bilayer selectively permeable?
check.referenceAnswer: The hydrophobic fatty acid interior resists polar and charged substances, so only some small nonpolar molecules pass easily.
check.feedback: The interior core is the key barrier, especially for charged and polar molecules.

items.essentialIdea: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy.

check.title: Passive Movement in Cells
check.prompt: What defines passive transport in terms of energy use and direction?
check.referenceAnswer: Passive transport moves substances from higher to lower concentration and does not require cellular energy.
check.feedback: It follows the gradient rather than using energy to move against it.

recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement best describes active transport?
choices: It moves substances from lower to higher concentration using cellular energy.
It moves substances from higher to lower concentration without cellular energy.
It only occurs through the phospholipid bilayer's hydrophobic interior.
It always moves oxygen and carbon dioxide in the same direction.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: It moves substances from lower to higher concentration using cellular energy.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Active transport requires energy and moves against the concentration gradient.
